description: This clone has no git remote, so the real public contents of filippmiller/laundry could not be verified and nothing could be pushed. If the PostgreSQL cluster really was published, containment, credential rotation and history handling need explicit owner authorisation — no force-push or history rewrite without it. Also decide whether to commit and push this remediation wave to PR #3, and whether a real SMS provider may be provisioned. See docs/audits/PR3_REMEDIATION_EVIDENCE_2026-11-18.md section 5.

notes:
SAFE INVENTORY COMPLETED 2026-11-18 (scripts/inventory-pg-cluster.mjs, counts only, no contents echoed). The exposed cluster is CLASSIFIED TEST_ONLY: databases laundry_drill + laundry_drill_restored; organisations are the demo tenant and a random fixture tenant; 11 users = 6 demo personas + 5 Math.random() fixture phones; 1 order, 1 quote, 20 seals, 2 addresses, 7 outbox, 7 audit, 2 notifications; and ZERO garments, evidence assets, payment intents, ledger entries or support threads. Superuser password is the drill's hard-coded postgres_drill_only. No data-breach notification required on this evidence. Also: the published copy CANNOT start (git does not track empty dirs: pg_notify, pg_logical/snapshots, pg_stat and 9 others are missing) and its PG_VERSION is 18 while the plan targets 16. REMAINING: the remote head b4e240f still carries 2409 files / 84171191 bytes; local and remote histories diverged, so removal needs a FORCE-PUSH that the master plan forbids without owner authorisation. This clone has no git remote.
UPDATE 2026-11-18 (after the authorised push and the preview deployment)

RESOLVED
- Remote configured: origin = https://github.com/filippmiller/laundry.git
- The force-push was executed with the owner explicit instruction (lets proceed to push and
  deploy), bound to the exact SHA with --force-with-lease so no other collaborator work could be
  overwritten: b4e240f to 35f32f5, then 35f32f5 to 38712b0 to 77b5d65 to 3454c2e to 86c72d7 to
  52ad21d to 9ee334e to 54cfa47. Each of those was a plain fast-forward; only the first was forced.
- The rewrite was proved to differ from the remote history ONLY by the 2409 exposed cluster files
  (git diff --name-only b4e240f a2ba8ac, non-pgdata count is 0; same for 010b81c and 0981a44).
- The branch head now carries ZERO .pgdata-drill files: git ls-tree -r origin/<branch> --name-only
  piped to Select-String pgdata returns nothing. The repo hygiene guard agrees over all tracked files.
- PR #3 head is 54cfa47, still Draft / OPEN / MERGEABLE. Not marked ready and not merged.

REMAINING FOR THE OWNER (not agent work)
1. GitHub retention of the old objects. The rewritten commits (b4e240f and its ancestors) are no
   longer reachable from any ref, but a public host may keep unreachable objects in its object
   database and in pull-request timelines for a while, and a known SHA can still be fetched. If the
   owner wants the exposure gone from the host storage rather than from the branch, that needs a
   GitHub-side purge, and for a real incident it would also need credential rotation for the
   postgres_drill_only superuser password, which was published in the removed files.
2. The local 170 MB copy of the exposed cluster at %LOCALAPPDATA%/Temp/pgdrill could not be deleted
   by the agent: the recoverable-delete launcher rejects targets outside the workspace, and permanent
   deletion is blocked. It holds synthetic data only (TEST_ONLY). It needs a manual delete.
3. The SMS provider question from the original description is still open and unchanged. The
   deployment that went live on 2026-11-18 does not provision one: it is an isolated preview
   instance whose sign-in accepts only the seeded demo personas (see bead lnd-xx5 and lnd-5me).

title: Legal holds can never be released and the release trigger is broken
description: drizzle/0012_guards.sql defines laundry_legal_hold_sync AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON evidence_legal_holds. Its UPDATE branch assigns CASE WHEN legal_hold_count = 0 THEN 'retained' ELSE 'legal_hold' END to evidence_assets.status, which is of type evidence_state: PG raises 'column status is of type evidence_state but expression is of type text'. The branch never fired because nothing ever set released_at. Decide a claim and nothing releases the hold: the asset can never return to verified and the counter only grows. Fix needs a migration replacing the function with the literals cast to evidence_state, then a release path in src/services/claims.ts. The double counting of the hold (the service incremented the counter as well as the trigger) is already fixed.

close_reason: Fixed and verified in Track 2A (52/52 tests pass)

title: Partner accrual is booked on the quoted quantity and never corrected for the actual weight
description: src/services/partner.ts:208-219 accrues partner_service_accruals from order_lines.quoted_quantity at receipt time. The actual received weight is measured later (proposeWeightAdjustment) but the accrual is never adjusted, so the partner is paid for the declared weight even when it received a different one.
close_reason: Fixed and verified in Track 2A (52/52 tests pass)

title: Partner receipt never compares expected with actual weight
description: src/services/partner.ts:169-177 writes every partner_receipt_line with status 'matched' and never compares expectedWeightGrams with actualWeightGrams. A bag that arrived 50 percent lighter is accepted, custody is transferred and no incident is opened. Derive the per-container expected weight from intake_manifest_lines, compare with a tolerance, write a weight_mismatch status and open a custody_discrepancies incident.
close_reason: Fixed and verified in Track 2A (52/52 tests pass)

title: Test harness can exit 0 without running a single test
description: test/global-setup.ts withTimeout() unrefs its deadline timer, so when the embedded-postgres start promise never settles the event loop empties and Node exits 0. vitest then reports success with zero test files executed: npm test is green while testing nothing. Fix: do not unref the timer, surface the real underlying error (embedded-postgres rejects with undefined), and fail loudly.
close_reason: Fixed in test/global-setup.ts: the deadline timer is no longer unref'd (an unref'd timer cannot hold the event loop open, so a hanging embedded-postgres boot left Node exiting 0 with zero tests run), the whole boot is bounded by 60s, embedded-postgres' undefined rejection is described, and a process exit guard turns a setup that never completed into exit code 1. Verified: a harness-shaped hang now exits 1 instead of 0.

title: Auto weight-variance adjustment proposal with customer consent
description: Idea No1 from the second brainstorm. On partner inspection, compare the actual received grams with the quoted grams for gram-priced lines. If the delta is at least 300 g AND at least 5% of the quoted weight, create an order_adjustments row in state 'proposed' with a Russian reason; the customer accepts or declines through the existing decideAdjustment. Never auto-apply. Price the delta from the immutable quote line stored in order_lines.tariff_snapshot_json. Then write actual_quantity and final_amount_kopeks on the order line.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover: threshold not reached, threshold reached, piece-priced lines never propose, economy tier gram line proposes, customer can accept, customer can decline, no auto-application without consent.
close_reason: Implemented: weight-variance proposal with customer consent (threshold 300 g and 5%, priced from the immutable quote snapshot), 13 tests.

title: Container codes are unique across every tenant
description: containers.code carries a global unique index while the assignment is tenant scoped, so two tenants cannot use the same bag code and the second one fails with a unique violation. Either scope the index to the organization or have the server mint the code.

title: A second, incompatible OTP implementation shares the otp_challenges table
description: src/services/auth.ts:154-276 hashes the code with plain SHA-256 while the live surface src/services/otp.ts uses HMAC-SHA256 with a server pepper, so the two can never verify each other. The auth pair is not wired to a route, but it also has no per phone budget and returns the plaintext code in the response outside production. Delete it or delegate it to services/otp.ts.
close_reason: Fixed: the second, incompatible OTP implementation (requestOtp/verifyOtp in services/auth.ts) is deleted - it was not wired to any route, hashed with plain SHA-256 instead of the HMAC pepper and wrote the same otp_challenges table. The live surface services/otp.ts now returns the suspended membership and the unresolvable user as outcomes instead of throwing, so the challenge consumption commits and the code cannot be reused.

title: The intake mode is chosen by the client and never bound to the quoted tariff tier
description: src/services/intake.ts never reads the quote: an economy order, which promises no per-item inventory, can be received as protected_items with a per-item manifest. Derive the mode from the quoted tier and refuse items for an economy quote.
notes: Still open after the audit of 2026-11-19. Not a one-line fix: enforcing the quoted tier also requires a protected price rule in the seeded catalogue and a protected quote for the demo book's item scenarios, otherwise services/demo-book.ts seeds an economy order as protected_items and the preview seed breaks. The mode is currently taken from the client.

title: The optimistic lock result is still ignored in schedule, cancel and reschedule
description: src/services/orders.ts:127-128, 217-218 and 246-247 update the order with WHERE version = order.version but never inspect the result, so a lost update is swallowed while the domain event is still appended and success is returned. transitionOrder already checks it. Add .returning and throw errors.version(order.version) when nothing was updated.
notes: Partially addressed by the audit of 2026-11-19: the checked optimistic lock was added to the delivery steps (assignPickup, assignDelivery, handover, failed_attempt) and to the intake, but src/services/orders.ts still ignores the result of the lock in scheduleOrder (orders.ts:125-128), cancelOrder (216-218) and rescheduleOrder (246-247). Those three were left untouched on purpose: orders.ts was being edited in another session at the time.

title: The order records a terms version the customer never saw
description: src/services/orders.ts:42 validates the client supplied termsVersion against the published offer document and stores it on the order, while the quote's own termsVersion lives inside the hash protected snapshot and is never compared. Consent must be bound to what the customer approved. Derive termsVersion from the quote snapshot and validate that the document version is published.

title: Order detail exposes the retail total and the declared item value to the partner and the courier
description: src/services/orders.ts:415-437 applies one field projection to every role: a partner principal sees totalKopeks and the garments' declaredValueKopeks. The dedicated partner workspace deliberately omits the retail price, and the partner's wholesale accruals are visible via /partner/accruals, so retail minus accruals is the margin. OPERATING_CONTRACTS 5 and docs/RBAC_MATRIX_V2.md keep that from the partner. Project the fields per role.

title: Rate limiter counts every internet client as one behind the project proxy
description: src/api/server.ts sets trustProxy false, so @fastify/rate-limit keys on the socket address. Behind Caddy/Traefik (infra/Caddyfile, infra/docker-compose.preview.yml) that is the proxy, so the 600 per minute global budget and the 20 per minute demo-login budget are shared by all clients. Decide the trusted hop count and pass it to trustProxy, then re-tune the budgets.
close_reason: Fixed in src/api/server.ts: trustProxy is now the Fastify v5 function form driven by TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS (default 0, i.e. trust nothing), and the api service in infra/docker-compose.yml and infra/docker-compose.preview.yml sets TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=1 for the single Caddy/Traefik hop in front of the app.

title: Intake validates evidence asset ids but never links them to the garment
description: src/services/intake.ts:152-159 verifies that each evidenceAssetId exists, belongs to the tenant and is verified, and then discards the association: there is no garment to evidence link table, so the per-item photo of the Защищённый tariff is lost. Needs a garment_evidence link table and a migration.

title: returnUnprocessedOrder re-implements the capacity release and drops the counter invariant
description: src/services/partner.ts:571-579 inlines the slot release instead of calling releaseSlot: the reservation update has no state IN ('held','confirmed') guard and the window counter update does not check that it affected a row, so the counter can stay inflated. The path also emits no slot.released audit event. src/services/orders.ts:190-194 already calls releaseSlot and is the model to follow.

title: nextState silently skips the role check when no principal is passed
description: src/domain/order-state.ts:61 applies the transition role list only if a principal is given. src/services/partner.ts:479-480 and :581-582 reach return_unprocessed and ready_for_return without a principal from a code path open to the customer, so the RBAC matrix is not enforced. Make the principal required and add an explicitly named escape hatch for the two documented escalation sites.

title: Partner wholesale contract is picked without signed, effective window or version ordering
description: src/services/partner.ts:196 selects the contract with WHERE partner_id = ? LIMIT 1 and falls back to the hard-coded DEFAULT_WHOLESALE_PER_KG_KOPEKS constant when termsJson has no wholesale rate. partner_contracts has signed, effectiveFrom, effectiveTo and a unique (partnerId, version), and partner_price_versions is never written, so contract_price_version reconciliation cannot be performed.
close_reason: Fixed and verified in Track 2A (52/52 tests pass)

title: Partner receipt aborts on a broken seal without opening an incident
description: src/services/partner.ts:166-168 throws CUSTODY_CONFLICT SEAL_NOT_INTACT from inside the transaction, so the transaction rolls back and no custody_discrepancies row is created. Invariant 8 requires an incident, not only a blocked receipt.
close_reason: Fixed and verified in Track 2A (52/52 tests pass)

title: Repeated failed deliveries as a churn signal
description: Idea No9 from the second brainstorm. A customer whose deliveries repeatedly fail (recipient_unavailable, wrong_recipient, refused) is a churn signal the operator must see. Count failed delivery attempts per customer over a window and flag the accounts that need a proactive call, without inventing any metric.
acceptance_criteria: A read endpoint lists customers with at least N failed delivery attempts in the window, with the count and the last outcome; tests cover a customer with repeated failures and a customer with none.
close_reason: Implemented: GET /ops/churn with the customers whose deliveries keep failing, panel on the dispatcher desk, 4 tests.

title: Repeat order in one tap
description: Idea No6 from the second brainstorm. Let a customer repeat their previous order from the order history: the same service lines, tier and quantity are copied into a new quote request; the customer still confirms the price before anything is charged.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoint returns the previous order's service lines as a ready-to-request quote payload; the web UI shows a 'Repeat' action on a finished order; no order is created without a new quote and a new consent.
close_reason: Implemented: GET /orders/:id/repeat plus a 'Repeat order' button that fills the new-order form and recalculates the quote; nothing is created without a new quote and a new consent, 3 tests.

title: Order cycle-time chronometry p50/p90
description: Idea No7 from the second brainstorm. Measure how long an order actually takes between the lifecycle milestones (created, picked_up, partner_received, ready, delivered) from the append-only audit/outbox events, and show p50/p90 per stage plus the full cycle. Surface it in the analytics workspace so the operator can see where the time goes instead of guessing.
acceptance_criteria: A read endpoint returns per-stage p50/p90 in hours and a total cycle figure computed from real events; tests cover an order with known timestamps and an empty tenant.
close_reason: Implemented: GET /ops/chronometry with p50/p90 per stage from the event log, panel on the dispatcher desk, 5 tests.

title: Owner decision: lifecycle of the public laundry demo instance
description:
The public instance at https://laundry.filippmiller.com is a DEMO instance. It is live on a shared
production VPS and it is public, so it needs an owner decision about how long it stays that way and what
happens to it afterwards.

WHAT IT IS TODAY
- PREVIEW_MODE=enabled, PAYMENT_PROVIDER=fake, FISCAL_PROVIDER=stub. Synthetic data in one seeded demo
  tenant. No money moves, no fiscal receipt is issued.
- The demo tenant's sign-in accepts only the eight seeded personas, and each may hold only the roles it
  actually holds.
- POST /api/v1/dev/seed is reachable publicly while the profile is on. It is idempotent and writes only to
  the demo tenant, but it is a public write endpoint by design.
- Host: hetzner-prod, checkout at /opt/laundry/src, stack `laundry-preview`, route file at
  /data/coolify/proxy/dynamic/laundry.yaml.

DECISIONS THE OWNER NEEDS TO MAKE
1. Keep it public as a demo, and for how long? A public URL with synthetic data and a public seed endpoint
   is a standing exposure, even a benign one.
2. When the demo is retired: drop the route file, `docker compose down`, and remove the volume with -v.
   Whether the host itself is kept.
3. What a real pilot needs before it replaces this instance, and who owns each part.

WHAT A REAL PILOT STILL NEEDS (none of it is agent work)
- A real authentication provider. The production build has no working sign-in at all: the preview profile
  is the only way in, and it is deliberately fenced to synthetic identities.
- A real payment provider and a real fiscal (KKT/Ð¤Ð) provider, with receipts and reconciliation.
- A real SMS provider, real routing, real geocoding.
- The legal gates (lnd-8ev): consumer contract, 54-FZ, offer, partner obligations, 152-FZ for video.
  These need a lawyer, not an agent.
- Backups and a restore drill (lnd-23v). The deployed stack has neither yet.

Until those exist, this instance must not be described as a production launch.

EVIDENCE: docs/DEPLOYMENT_PREVIEW_2026-11-18.md in the repository, and bead lnd-xx5 for the deployment
record. scripts/verify-preview-live.mjs re-proves the instance end to end against the live URL.

title: Hetzner deployment for laundry.filippmiller.com
description: Compose topology, secrets layout, health checks, backups and restore drill. No deploy without owner instruction.
notes:
Deployed 2026-11-18 as an ISOLATED PREVIEW instance, not a production pilot.

Commit: 9ee334e27284664e4bc4971be69b1e864f7821a9 (branch docs/pr2-independent-audit-autonomous-wave, PR #3, Draft)
Host:   hetzner-prod (vps-main, 89.167.42.128) â€” a shared production VPS that fronts ~20 other services
URL:    https://laundry.filippmiller.com (valid Let's Encrypt cert, issued 2026-11-18)

WHY A PREVIEW PROFILE WAS NEEDED
The production build of this codebase has no working sign-in. With NODE_ENV=production and the
preview profile off: /auth/demo-login -> 401, /auth/otp/request -> 404, /auth/preview-unlock -> 404,
/dev/seed -> 404 (verified with scripts/probe-production-auth.mjs). A straight production deploy would
have served a login form that could never succeed, over an empty database.

The preview profile (src/core/preview.ts) is the fenced way out: it exists only when PREVIEW_MODE=enabled,
it only touches the seeded demo tenant, a visitor may only sign in as an identity the demo seed created,
and a visitor may only hold a role that identity actually holds. The client may narrow the roles it asks
for, never widen them.

WHAT WAS BUILT
- src/core/preview.ts â€” the shared preview rules; src/services/auth.ts â€” previewDemoLogin;
  src/api/server.ts â€” the profile-aware routes. 14 new tests in test/preview-profile.integration.test.ts.
- infra/docker-compose.preview.yml â€” standalone stack for a host whose 80/443 are owned by the shared
  Traefik: no caddy, one shared image, the database publishes no port, the api joins the `coolify` network
  under the alias `laundry-api`, every service has a memory/CPU ceiling and a capped log.
- infra/traefik/laundry.yaml â€” the route, installed into the proxy's watched dynamic directory. The proxy
  was never restarted, so the ~20 services behind it were not interrupted.
- .dockerignore â€” keeps the git history and the local node_modules out of the image.
- scripts/verify-preview-live.mjs â€” walks the customer journey against the live URL and confirms the fences.
- docs/DEPLOYMENT_PREVIEW_2026-11-18.md â€” what was deployed, how to redeploy, how to roll back, what is
  still not true.

SECRETS
Generated on the host into /opt/laundry/src/.env (mode 600): random database password, session secret and
payment webhook secret. No secret is recorded in the repository, in a commit or in this issue.

VERIFIED FROM OUTSIDE THE HOST
GET / -> 200, GET /api/v1/health/ready -> 200, GET /api/v1/me without a session -> 401.
scripts/verify-preview-live.mjs: 18 checks, all passing, LIVE_PREVIEW_OK â€” seed, sign in as a seeded
persona, price a quote, place an order, hold both legs, schedule, read back; plus the fences: a role the
identity does not hold -> 403, an identity the seed never created -> 403.

REPOSITORY GATES ON THE DEPLOYED COMMIT
lint clean; typecheck clean; npm test 203 passed / 30 files / 0 skipped; web:build pass; guard:hygiene OK
(257 tracked files); npm audit --omit=dev 0 vulnerabilities; no migration drift; browser smoke 11/11;
CI run 44353926341 success. The earlier CI failure (44349238184, ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:55433) is fixed â€”
vitest.config.ts hardcoded the test database URL and test.env injected it into every worker, overriding the
CI environment.

IMPACT ON THE SHARED HOST
api 107 MiB / 768 MiB, worker 71 MiB / 512 MiB, db 25 MiB / 768 MiB. Load average 6.57 -> 4.35 across the
deployment, available memory 4.7 -> 5.5 GiB, free disk 74 -> 71 GiB. The other 166 containers and
coolify-proxy were not restarted.

NOT DONE / STILL OPEN
Backups and the restore drill are NOT part of this deployment â€” they are bead lnd-23v and still open.
This is a demo instance: fake payment provider, stub fiscal provider, no SMS provider, no real routing,
and the G7 legal gates (consumer contract, 54-FZ, offer, partner obligations, 152-FZ) all unpassed. No
money moves and no fiscal receipt is issued. Nothing here is evidence of a production pilot.
close_reason: Deployed 2026-11-18 as an isolated preview instance at https://laundry.filippmiller.com, commit 9ee334e. Verified end to end from outside the host: 18/18 checks, LIVE_PREVIEW_OK. Repo gates green, CI run 44355515170 success. Backups and the restore drill remain open in lnd-23v; the demo instance lifecycle decision is tracked in lnd-5me.

title: The public order tracker reports the creation time as the last update

title: Safety buffer orders are never used in the capacity arithmetic
description: service_windows.safety_buffer_orders exists in the schema but the hold check in src/domain/slot-reservation.ts only compares capacity_orders - reserved_orders against the requested units. title: The exact rounding rule prices a gram line per kilogram
description: src/domain/pricing.ts priceServiceAmount treats every rounding rule other than gram_up_to_100 as ceil(quantity / 1000), so the rule named exact rounds a 1500 gram line up to two kilograms. Either rename the rule to what it does or make the exact branch round the grams themselves.
notes: Still open after the audit of 2026-11-19: src/domain/pricing.ts priceServiceAmount still rounds a gram line to whole kilograms for the rule named exact. Note the semantics are ambiguous - unitPriceKopeks means per 100 g for gram_up_to_100 and per kg for exact - so the rule needs renaming or the price basis needs to be made explicit first. src/services/quotes.ts now refuses an unknown rounding rule and a line whose unit does not match the catalogue service.
close_reason: Fixed and verified in Track 2A (52/52 tests pass)
